answer: One practical defense is requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake tied to a persistent identity record before it can transact. A swarm of fake accounts then gets expensive fast, since every clone needs its own stake, and bad behavior burns the deposit instead of just spawning a new name. Think of it like quartz veins in a dune field: the real deposits are sparse and costly to dig, while at the zenith of a fake swarm the clones hold nothing scarce, so peers can spot and ignore them.
